question: Which 5 customers have spent the most?
sql: WITH cust_spend AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, COALESCE(SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity), 0) AS total_spent, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.id AND o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.id, c.name), ranked AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_spent DESC) AS rnk FROM cust_spend) SELECT id, name, total_spent, cancelled_orders FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 5 ORDER BY total_spent DESC, id LIMIT 100

question: What share of total revenue does each product category contribute?
sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS revenue, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) / (SELECT SUM(oi2.unit_price * oi2.quantity) FROM order_items AS oi2 JOIN orders AS o2 ON oi2.order_id = o2.id WHERE o2.status <> 'cancelled'), 2) AS revenue_share_percent, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled') AS cancelled_orders FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category LIMIT 100
answer: Accessories account for 10.26% of total revenue, Electronics for 45.59%, Furniture for 41.08%, and Stationery for 3.07%.

question: Which product has sold the most units?
sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT oi.product_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY oi.product_id), cancelled AS (SELECT oi.product_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS cancelled_units FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY oi.product_id), max_units AS (SELECT MAX(COALESCE(total_units, 0)) AS max_total FROM sold) SELECT p.name, COALESCE(s.total_units, 0) AS total_units, COALESCE(c.cancelled_units, 0) AS cancelled_orders FROM products AS p LEFT JOIN sold AS s ON p.id = s.product_id LEFT JOIN cancelled AS c ON p.id = c.product_id JOIN max_units AS m ON COALESCE(s.total_units, 0) = m.max_total LIMIT 100
answer: Notebook Set sold the most units, with 11 units sold.

sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, COALESCE(s.total_spend, 0) AS total_spend, COALESCE(co.cancelled_orders, 0) AS cancelled_orders, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(s.total_spend, 0) DESC) AS spend_rank FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_spend FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_id) AS s ON s.customer_id = c.id LEFT JOIN (SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS cancelled_orders FROM orders AS o WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_id) AS co ON co.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY total_spend DESC LIMIT 100
answer: The customers are ranked by total spend from highest to lowest, with Vikram Nair leading at Rs 33,895 (rank 1) and Aditya Bose at Rs 0 (rank 20).
reference_sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity), RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) DESC) FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.id

question: Which customers spent more than the average customer?
sql: WITH customer_spend AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, c.email, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN oi.unit_price * oi.quantity END), 0) AS total_spent, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email), avg_spend AS (SELECT AVG(total_spent) AS avg_spent FROM customer_spend) SELECT cs.id, cs.name, cs.email, cs.total_spent, cs.cancelled_orders FROM customer_spend AS cs CROSS JOIN avg_spend WHERE cs.total_spent > avg_spend.avg_spent LIMIT 100
answer: The customers who spent more than the average are Ananya Iyer (Rs 28,796), Dev Chauhan (Rs 21,999), Diya Patel (Rs 10,094), Pooja Desai (Rs 17,998), Rohan Mehta (Rs 17,498) and Vikram Nair (Rs 33,895).
reference_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) AS s FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name FROM t JOIN customers c ON c.id = t.customer_id WHERE t.s > (SELECT AVG(s) FROM t)

question: Who are our most valuable customers?
sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, c.email, COALESCE(SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity), 0) AS total_spent, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON c.id = o.customer_id LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.id = oi.order_id AND o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 100
answer: Your most valuable customers are Vikram Nair (Rs 33,895), Ananya Iyer (Rs 28,796) and Dev Chauhan (Rs 21,999).

question: Compare how the categories are performing.
sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN oi.unit_price * oi.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN oi.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_sold, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN o.id END) AS orders, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN o.id END) AS cancelled_orders FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category LIMIT 100
answer: Electronics is the top‑performing category with Rs 83,674 revenue, 26 units sold and 16 orders and no cancellations; Furniture follows with Rs 75,392 revenue but has 2 cancelled orders, while Accessories generates Rs 18,834 from 16 units and 9 orders, and Stationery trails with Rs 5,630 from 20 units and 4 orders.

question: Who are the top 3 customers by total spend?
sql: WITH cust_spend AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, COALESCE(SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity), 0) AS total_spend, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.id AND o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.id, c.name), ranked AS (SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_spend DESC) AS rnk FROM cust_spend) SELECT id, name, total_spend, cancelled_orders FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 3 ORDER BY total_spend DESC, id LIMIT 100
answer: The top three customers by total spend are Vikram Nair (Rs 33,895), Ananya Iyer (Rs 28,796) and Dev Chauhan (Rs 21,999).
reference_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) AS s FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name FROM t JOIN customers c ON c.id = t.customer_id ORDER BY t.s DESC LIMIT 3

question: Which product has sold the most units?
sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT p.id, p.name, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN oi.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_sold, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN oi.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM products AS p LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name), max_sales AS (SELECT MAX(units_sold) AS max_units FROM sales) SELECT s.name, s.units_sold, s.cancelled_orders FROM sales AS s CROSS JOIN max_sales AS m WHERE s.units_sold = m.max_units LIMIT 100
answer: The Notebook Set sold the most units, with 11 units sold.
reference_sql: SELECT p.name FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.id HAVING SUM(i.quantity) = (SELECT MAX(u) FROM (SELECT SUM(i2.quantity) AS u FROM order_items i2 JOIN orders o2 ON o2.id = i2.order_id WHERE o2.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY i2.product_id))

question: List every possible pair of two different customers.
sql: SELECT c1.id AS customer1_id, c1.name AS customer1_name, c2.id AS customer2_id, c2.name AS customer2_name FROM customers AS c1 JOIN customers AS c2 ON c1.id < c2.id LIMIT 100
answer: The result lists distinct customer pairs, beginning with Aarav Sharma paired with every other customer and then Diya Patel paired with Rohan Mehta, and so on. Only the first 20 of the 100 possible pairs are shown because the query’s LIMIT was reached.
reference_sql: SELECT a.name, b.name FROM customers a JOIN customers b ON a.id != b.id

question: List every combination of an order ID and a product name.
sql: SELECT orders.id AS order_id, products.name AS product_name FROM orders JOIN order_items ON orders.id = order_items.order_id JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.id LIMIT 100
answer: The result shows each order ID paired with the product names it contains (e.g., order 1 includes “Wireless Mouse” and “Notebook Set”, order 2 includes “Noise Cancelling Headphones”, etc.). Only the first 20 of the 47 matching rows are displayed.
reference_sql: SELECT o.id, p.name FROM orders o CROSS JOIN products p
